clue.text: A lot of stuff in joker's come-back gets a laugh

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round
a come-back returns, so the word for the joker is read backwards

parts.note: a wag is a joker or wit

indicators.note: most of the word stuff is taken, its last three letters, not the whole

explanation.surface: A comedian's clever retort full of material wins over the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of stuff' takes only the last three of its five letters. 'come-back' reverses the joker; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A guffaw is a loud hearty burst of laughter, so the noun stands for what the clue's verb phrase earns.

clue.text: Fruit and sticky things I start to gobble

parts.note: goos are sticky substances
ego is Latin for I, the self

indicators.note: the start of the word gobble gives its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone eats fruit and sticky sweets, beginning to wolf them down.
explanation.walkthrough: GOOSEGOG is British slang for gooseberry.
explanation.definitionFit: A gooseberry is a tart green fruit, and the slang name is a dialect variant.

clue.text: Small portion's right out for a party!

indicators.note: out means the letter for right is removed

parts.note: a fraction is a small portion

explanation.surface: A small share of something is withdrawn from a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes R from FRACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A faction is a dissenting group within a larger body, a party in that sense.

clue.text: No, I'd interrupt a lot, sounding very nasal

indicators.note: the letters break into the phrase meaning a lot

parts.note: a deal means a lot, as in a good deal
taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone protests that they would not keep cutting in, and speaks very nasally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupt' puts NOID inside A DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An adenoidal voice sounds blocked and through the nose, as with enlarged adenoids.

clue.text: I'll see new York, shortly, recollecting old ways

indicators.note: read as re-collecting, gathering the letters together again in a new order

parts.note: York cut short to its initial gives Y

explanation.surface: Someone planning a trip to York remembers the ancient tracks of the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollecting' shuffles ILLSEE with N and Y. Ley lines are supposed alignments of ancient sites across the British landscape, believed by some to be old tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ley lines are imagined prehistoric routes linking ancient monuments, so they are taken here as ancient paths.

clue.text: Dairy product presented in talk? Overpaid me, in error

indicators.note: in error means wrongly, so these letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a dairy product was mis-priced, saying 'You overpaid me'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' shuffles TALK and OVERPAIDME together.
explanation.definitionFit: Evaporated milk is concentrated tinned milk with much of its water removed.

clue.text: Source of gold in rich vein accounts for the cabin

indicators.note: the source of gold sits inside the word for the vein

parts.note: a lode is a rich vein of ore

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gold strike in a rich seam pays for a prospector's cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of' gives G; 'in' puts it inside LODE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodge is a small country house or hut, such as a hunting lodge.

clue.text: A small compartment in rear portion of plane?

definitions.text: A small compartment in rear portion of plane?

indicators.note: the compartment is placed inside the letters from the end of the plane
the rear portion of the word plane is its last two letters

parts.note: a cell is a small compartment

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether there is a little storage area at the back of the aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear portion of' here takes the last two letters of 'plane', not just one. A nacelle is the casing round an aircraft engine, so the whole clue also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacelle is a streamlined housing on an aircraft for an engine or crew.

clue.text: Rascal's taken to one type of sea food

parts.note: a scamp is a rascal
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A mischievous rascal takes a liking to a certain seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustines or large prawns, fried in breadcrumbs as a dish.

clue.text: Nick heard enthusing about English printing method

indicators.note: heard means the word for stealing is given by how it sounds

parts.note: to nick is to steal
raving about something is enthusing about it

explanation.surface: A thief is overheard praising an English way of printing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' works on the word for Nick alone; 'enthusing about' is one phrase, and its synonym follows the English abbreviation in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel engraving is a technique for printing images from incised steel plates.

clue.text: Band of gold depicted on breast by artist

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
the chest is the breast
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A gold band is painted over someone's heart in a portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a ring of gold; it is a group of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of musicians playing together, which is a band in the musical sense.

clue.text: Yes, Russian tea may be found in this cottage

parts.note: da is Russian for yes
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A visitor learns that Russian tea is served in a country cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country house or summer cottage.

clue.text: I'll be in record book as a prime example

indicators.note: the letter is to be put inside the record and book

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
a tome is a large book
I, taken from I'll, the 'll being part of the indicator

explanation.surface: Someone boasts they will appear in a record book as the perfect specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll be in' reads as a boast, but it splits: I is the piece and 'be in' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect representative of a type, the model case of something.

clue.text: Performances of bowler and miler have something in common

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls delivered by one bowler
a lap of the track is a stage run by a miler, a middle-distance runner

explanation.surface: A cricketer's and a runner's efforts are compared and found similar.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER is six deliveries bowled in cricket; a miler runs four laps of a track.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that overlap share some part or area, coinciding in part.

clue.text: Had nothing new brought in to get married

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: the letters for nothing and new are carried inside the word for marrying

parts.note: to wed is to get married

explanation.surface: Someone with nothing new to offer is pressed into a marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' puts ON inside WED.
explanation.definitionFit: Had in the sense of possessed: to have owned something is to have held it as property.

clue.text: One may scan the papers with passing interest

definitions.text: One may scan the papers with passing interest

parts.words: One may scan the papers with passing interest
parts.note: reads as a casual newspaper reader, but the papers are exam papers and the interest is in passing the test

explanation.surface: A commuter idly glances over the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate sitting an exam reads the question papers hoping for a pass.

clue.text: Bury forward has to fit in with the rest

parts.note: to inter is to bury
a lock is a forward in rugby, a second-row player

explanation.surface: A footballer from Bury, a northern English club, fits well into the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the English town and football club; it is the verb. A lock is a rugby forward position.
explanation.definitionFit: Parts that interlock join closely together, engaging with one another.

clue.text: Modified gun inlay is rather clumsy

indicators.note: modified means altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gun with decorative inlay is a bit awkward to handle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungainly means awkward and lacking grace in movement.

clue.text: Good golfer's record mentioned in introduction

parts.note: a pro is a professional, a good golfer

indicators.note: spoken, so the word for a record is given by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A golfing professional's scorecard is cited in the opening remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mentioned' signals that LOGUE is pronounced like LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A prologue is the opening section that sets up a play or book, a preface.

clue.text: Right colour for linen — it's for a cadet, perhaps

parts.note: ecru is the greyish-yellow colour of unbleached linen
it, the 's being part of the link

explanation.surface: A decision about the proper shade of linen for a cadet's uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A recruit is a newly enlisted member, and a cadet is one example of a trainee.

clue.text: I may be put in a shift in the city…

indicators.note: the I is placed inside the word for a shift

parts.note: a turn is a shift or spell of duty

explanation.surface: A worker says they might be assigned to a shift in the city, leading on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be put in' puts I inside TURN. The ellipsis just links this clue's surface to 23 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city of north-west Italy.

clue.text: He'll have shot his bolt

parts.note: the idiom means exhausted his efforts, but literally a worker who fires rivets drives bolts home

explanation.surface: Someone will have used up all their strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A riveter is a worker who fastens metal plates with rivets, metal bolts driven in.

clue.text: Nothing kept in an apartment aboard ship?

parts.note: taken as A

indicators.note: the letter for nothing is held inside the words for an apartment

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An empty apartment on a ship is left with nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept in' puts O inside A FLAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something afloat is floating on water, as one is when at sea on a vessel.

clue.text: …if such a processing plant appears

indicators.note: processing works the letters over into a new form

explanation.surface: Continuing the story: if a processing factory is built, then something follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' reads as a factory with 'processing'; it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuchsia is a shrub with drooping purple and red flowers.

clue.text: Smart man wants to expand

explanation.surface: A dapper gentleman is keen to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A swell is a dandy or stylish person; to swell is to increase in size.

clue.text: Excellent "no 5" scent almost rejected in Czech region

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written with the figure 1 as I
number five in Roman numerals is V

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an aroma is a scent

explanation.surface: A famous perfume called No 5 is turned down in a Czech region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims AROMA to AROM; 'rejected' turns AI + V + AROM into MORAVIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Moravia is a historic area of the eastern Czech Republic.

clue.text: Egg appropriate to festive season, it's said

indicators.note: spoken, so the phrase meaning of Christmas is given by its sound

parts.note: of Yule, Yule being the Christmas season

explanation.surface: An egg suits the holiday period, according to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' signals that OVULE sounds like 'of Yule'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovule is the structure that develops into a seed, a small egg in botany or zoology.

clue.text: I'll try backing kind of profit made dishonestly

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
a go is a try

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word for the profit is turned round

parts.note: nett profit is the profit after deductions

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to reverse a certain kind of profit that was earned crookedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns NETT into TTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-gotten gains are acquired by unfair or crooked means.

clue.text: Training in France, you had note about strong wind returning

parts.note: tu is the French for you

indicators.note: the note goes around the wind word

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the wind word is read backwards

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: Someone recalls being taught in France amid a story about a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses the wind and 'about' wraps the note round it. 'had' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is instruction or guidance given by a tutor.

clue.text: Stray into Scottish island, mostly rocky one

indicators.note: the word for straying goes inside the island
most of the word, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Skye is an island of the Inner Hebrides
to err is to stray

explanation.surface: Someone wanders onto a Scottish island, which is largely rocky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stray' looks like an anagram signal but is the verb meaning wander. 'mostly' trims the island; 'into' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A skerry is a small reef or rocky islet, so it is an island made of rock.
